clue.text: Eccentric partisan

definitions.meaning: something eccentric is odd, out of the normal pattern
a partisan is a guerrilla fighter, a soldier outside the regular army

explanation.surface: A description of an odd, one-sided supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: odd or abnormal behaviour, and a guerrilla soldier not part of a formal army.

clue.text: Correct yet again about the current recession

parts.note: re is a short word meaning concerning or about

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the word for the current is read backwards

parts.note: the tide is the current of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone revising a report on the latest economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks like an economic downturn but signals going backwards, applied to the sea's current.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to correct text, and doing it once more is a second pass of revision.

clue.text: In time a little beast will make mistakes

indicators.note: the clue puts the little beast in time, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a small animal, a little beast

explanation.surface: A warning that given enough time, a small creature will blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a creature making errors; 'mistakes' is a plural noun, the list of printing slips.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for printing errors listed in a book.

clue.text: Having to push maybe in the end

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the words before it could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone eventually forced to give a shove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' reworks TO PUSH. The definition is adverbial but the noun means the final result, what happens in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or result of events is what comes about eventually.

clue.text: Mean to issue a statement before very long

indicators.note: the statement comes before the long time in the answer

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is informally a very long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: Someone intending to make an announcement shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend; it is the arithmetic average.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic norm of a set of values.

clue.text: Scoffed about the second being unduly complimented

indicators.note: the eating word goes about, around, the word for the second

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed can mean fed
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone mocking another while they receive excessive praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like jeered, but here it is British slang for eating hungrily; 'about' wraps the eating word round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Being praised excessively or insincerely is to be buttered up with compliments.

clue.text: Made a live broadcast in years gone by

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV crew who went out live in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a TV term but scatters MADEALIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval refers to the Middle Ages, a period long in the past.

clue.text: Watched outside event, as almost adult

indicators.note: the watched word goes outside, around the event

parts.note: seen is what has been watched

explanation.surface: A teenager seen standing outside an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; at seventeen one is a year short of eighteen, the usual age of adulthood in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seventeen is one year short of eighteen, the usual age of adulthood.

clue.text: Strip for run before church

indicators.note: the running word comes before the church abbreviation

parts.note: to flee is to run away
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting into church to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like undress; to fleece is to rob someone of their money.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle and rob them of everything they have.

clue.text: Urge getting into the action when feeling low

indicators.note: the urge is getting into, entering, the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Someone urged into activity when they feel down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone depressed is in low spirits, sad and dejected.

clue.text: Everybody out to make a hit

definitions.meaning: a call for all workers to down tools, a walkout
to hit something is to land a blow on it

explanation.surface: A union boss calling a walkout to score a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A union's walkout is industrial action, and to land a blow is the verb sense of hitting.

clue.text: It's just not true it can foil crooked characters

indicators.note: crooked means bent or twisted, so these letters are bent into another order

explanation.surface: A false claim that crooks can be thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges ITCANFOIL. The definition is a sentence describing something made up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fictional is invented, made up rather than factual.

clue.text: Abandon an unproductive piece of land

definitions.meaning: to abandon is to leave someone behind
an arid region where little grows

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to leave a barren plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave behind is the verb sense; an arid barren region is the noun sense.

clue.text: A dunderhead calling for the entree

parts.note: read as 'dunder head', the head or first letter of dunder
a mission is a calling or vocation

explanation.surface: An idiot with a vocation seeking access to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' means a fool, but cryptically it is the head of 'dunder'. 'Entree' means entry here, not a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is the right of access, the permission to enter somewhere.

clue.text: Contending with constituents is strange

indicators.note: constituents are the separate parts, so these letters are taken as components to reassemble

explanation.surface: An observation that arguing with one's voters is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' rearranges ISSTRANGE; it looks like voters in a political constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: Contending is maintaining or claiming something in argument.

clue.text: A flighty creature will supply all the runners with food

parts.note: the field is all the competitors in a race
fare is food provided

explanation.surface: A bird that feeds every competitor in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' looks like fickle but means able to fly; the fieldfare is a thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Allow for rent

definitions.meaning: to hire out property to a tenant

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are verbs: permit, and lease out property to a tenant.

clue.text: Some cattle ambling about in a field

indicators.note: some means a part of the words that follow, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: A herd wandering round a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'cattLE Ambling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or pasture.

clue.text: Add up for a child

definitions.meaning: to total figures, usually followed by 'up'

explanation.definitionFit: Total figures is the verb sense, and a toddler is the noun sense.

clue.text: Animosity can set the underworld boss corresponding

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld
like means similar or corresponding

explanation.surface: A gangland chief stirring up hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' looks like a crime lord; it is Dis, Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is hostility or aversion toward someone.

clue.text: Love to chatter about English work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the chatter word goes about, around, the English abbreviation

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly

explanation.surface: Someone who loves to gossip about English work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside PRATE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to work or function, as a machine does.

clue.text: Fit for a little exercise

parts.note: PT is physical training, a short school exercise session

explanation.surface: Someone getting fit through a bit of a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate for a purpose.

clue.text: Talk about the Spanish church dignitary

indicators.note: the talk word goes about, around, the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to talk idly
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Gossip about a Spanish bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk about' reads as a phrase but splits: the talk word goes about the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other senior cleric.

clue.text: One buys and sells most desirable models

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
to deal is to trade, buy and sell

explanation.surface: A trader handling top-end models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like cars or fashion; it means perfect examples to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection, the best examples to aim at.

clue.text: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)

definitions.text: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)

parts.words: Hail to thee, — Spirit! Bird thou never wert." Shelley (To a Skylark)
parts.note: the opening line of Shelley's poem To a Skylark with the adjective before Spirit left out, to be filled in

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the missing word from Shelley's famous opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley addresses the skylark as a cheerful, carefree spirit in the poem's first line.

clue.text: Look for the small change in a party

indicators.note: the change goes in, inside, the party words

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
p is a penny, small change

explanation.surface: Someone looking for loose coins at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside A SECT, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something.

clue.text: A Kipling novel turned up festive occasion for the emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the words read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Kipling book appearing at an imperial party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses A KIM into MIKA, followed by DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is a former title of the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Sensible article is well put together

indicators.note: the letters are put together again into a well-formed new order

explanation.surface: Praise for a sensible and well-structured piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well put together' rearranges ARTICLEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being realistic means practical and grounded, sensible about what is possible.

clue.text: Started as a bigwig in the Canterbury area

parts.note: SE is south-east England, where Canterbury in Kent lies
a toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: Someone who began life as a grandee in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a wealthy aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to start out on a journey.

clue.text: An American stock holder

parts.note: reads like an investor on Wall Street, but the stock is livestock held on a ranch

explanation.definitionFit: A rancher who raises livestock in the US is one who keeps cattle.

clue.text: They have to make news or bust!

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Newspaper proprietors who must make headlines or go bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' rearranges NEWSOR; it looks like bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who possess something are its proprietors.

clue.text: Keeping note X turned it on

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
X is ten in Roman numerals

indicators.note: turned means the two short words are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Someone holding on to a note marked X and switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges ITON into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of keeping or holding on to something.
